title: Labor-process demand can be substantial while durable worker power remains unmeasured
source_unit: National Labor Relations Board FY 2025 Performance and Accountability Report

denominator.unit: NLRB-reported unfair-labor-practice charges and representation petitions

contested_board_decisions.unit: decisions issued during periods with a quorum

board_quorum_context.value: lacked a quorum for nearly three-quarters of the fiscal year

observations.method: Review of NLRB's FY 2025 performance and accountability report, preserving charge, merit, settlement, petition, and Board-decision stages as separate administrative measures.
observations.uncertainty: Charges are allegations; merit and settlement measures have source-defined case universes; petitions do not necessarily become elections; reported output is shaped by delegation, settlement, staffing, and quorum conditions.
observations.subgroup: Private-sector employees, labor organizations, employers, unfair-labor-practice cases, and representation petitions within NLRB jurisdiction.
observations.counterinterpretation: High filings can reflect awareness or legal change rather than worsening workplaces; high settlement can reflect efficient resolution or limited adjudication; low Board decisions can reflect settlement or quorum constraints rather than low conflict.

related_sources.claim: NLRB publishes agency performance and election reports covering contested labor and representation cases.
NLRB publishes representation petition and election activity categories.

boundary: This record measures demand and output on a formal labor-administration route. It does not establish the prevalence of workplace violations, individual remedy receipt, bargaining outcomes, workplace improvement, union coverage, trust, or durable worker power.
